info.title: dixcord-bot webapi
info.description: Internal REST API backing the dixcord-bot Discord bot, webview, and webadmin services. Every route requires a service-account JWT (admin, bot, or webview) except login and health.

403.description: Service accounts cannot be deleted via the API.

get.description: Flat list of every trigger/response junction row, joined with its trigger and response text.

post.description: Requires the admin role. Convenience one-shot alternative to POST /api/trigger-responses/triggers: gets-or-creates the trigger (by trigger_string) and the response (by response_string), then links them with a new trigger_response row. Setting selection_mode here updates the trigger's mode.

get.description: Bare trigger text only (no ids), for the bot to match against message content.

post.summary: Create a trigger with a batch of responses
post.description: Requires the admin role. If trigger_string already exists, reuses that trigger (and updates its selection_mode) rather than creating a duplicate; response_string values are deduped the same way. Entries in responses missing a non-empty response_string are silently skipped.

selection_mode.description: Falls back to "random" if omitted or not one of the valid values.

201.description: Created (or reused) trigger with its responses.

get.summary: List all triggers with id and selection_mode
get.description: CRUD-oriented listing (unlike GET /api/trigger-responses/triggers, which returns bare strings). Registered before /triggers/{id} so the literal "list" segment is not shadowed by the id param route.

get.summary: Get all responses for a trigger, by trigger text or trigger id
get.description: Exactly one of `trigger` or `triggerId` must be supplied; `triggerId` takes precedence if both are present. Returns 400 if neither is given. Registered before /triggers/{id} so the literal "responses" segment is not shadowed by the id param route.

parameters.name: trigger
parameters.description: Trigger text. Ignored if triggerId is also given.

parameters.name: triggerId
parameters.description: Trigger id. Takes precedence over trigger if both are given.

get.summary: Get one trigger by id, with its responses

put.summary: Update a trigger's selection_mode and/or its response list
put.description: Requires the admin role. Each entry in `responses` is either `{ id: linkId, order?, weight? }` to update an existing trigger_response link's order/weight, or `{ response_string, order?, weight? }` to add a new response (deduped by response_string) to this trigger. Entries matching neither shape are silently skipped. Both fields are optional; an empty body is a no-op that still returns 200.

selection_mode.description: Falls back to "random" if not one of the valid values.

id.description: Existing trigger_response link id to update.

response_string.description: Adds a new response when id is not given.

200.description: The updated trigger with its responses.

delete.description: Requires the admin role. Removes all trigger_response links for this trigger, then deletes any responses that are left with no remaining links (orphan cleanup).

get.summary: Get one selected response for a trigger
get.description: Looks up the trigger by exact trigger_string and picks one response per its selection_mode: "random" (uniform DB-side random pick), "ordered" (round-robin by response_order, tracked in trigger_response_state), or "weighted" (weighted roll against each link's weight, 0-100). Selecting a response increments frequency counters on the trigger, response, and link rows. When app and userId are both supplied, also records a trigger_response_user_history row for the requesting user (resolved via chat_member_mapping); this is best-effort and silently skipped if the user isn't mapped yet, so it never affects the response returned.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: Chat app key for userId, e.g. "discord". Required (together with userId) to log history.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Platform user id (e.g. Discord snowflake) of the user receiving the response, for history logging.

404.description: No trigger matching trigger_string, or it has no responses.

get.description: Reads directly from the responses table (not the trigger_response junction).

put.description: Requires the admin role. Updates the shared responses row directly, so the new text applies to every trigger this response is linked to.

delete.description: Requires the admin role. Deletes the shared responses row; trigger_response links referencing it are removed via ON DELETE CASCADE, so this unlinks the response from every trigger that used it.

get.description: Catalog of prize keys usable as a weighted trigger response's trigger_response.lotto_prize value. The bot hydrates its in-process prize handler table from this list, matching each prize_string against a handler function; catalog rows with no matching handler are a no-op.

frequency.description: Times this prize has been awarded.

get.description: chatMemberId is the internal chat_member_mapping.id (as returned by GET /api/user-mappings), not a platform id. Entries are newest first, joined with trigger/response text for display.

parameters.name: chatMemberId

get.summary: Get one trigger-response link by id
get.description: Registered last among the GET routes on this router so more specific literal segments (/triggers, /triggers/list, /triggers/responses, /random, /responses/{id}) are matched first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: trigger_response junction row id (not a trigger id or response id).

put.description: Requires the admin role. All fields are optional but at least one must be given (400 otherwise). Setting trigger_string or response_string re-points the link at a get-or-created trigger/response (by string, deduped) rather than renaming the existing one in place. selection_mode is applied to the link's trigger. response_order and weight may be set to null to clear them.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: trigger_response junction row id.

trigger_string.description: Re-points the link at this (get-or-created) trigger.

response_string.description: Re-points the link at this (get-or-created) response.

delete.description: Requires the admin role. Removes only the trigger_response junction row; the underlying trigger and response rows are left in place (unlike DELETE /triggers/{id}, which also prunes orphaned responses).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: trigger_response junction row id.

get.summary: List scheduled messages (requester, bot, or admin scope)
get.description:
Behavior depends on `scope`:
  - Omitted (default, "requester scope"): resolves `requesterUserId` to a
    chat_member_mapping row and returns that single user's upcoming
    pending scheduled messages. Requires the bot or admin role (checked
    in-handler); callers other than the bot act on a user's behalf via
    `requesterUserId`.
  - `scope=bot`: returns every pending scheduled message for the app
    (all users), for the bot's own scheduler loop. Requires the bot
    role (checked in-handler); `requesterUserId` is ignored.
  - `scope=admin`: returns a paginated, `status`-filterable list across
    all users for the admin panel. Requires the admin role (checked
    in-handler); `requesterUserId` is ignored.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: Chat app key. Currently only "discord" is supported.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Selects bot or admin scope. Omit for requester scope.

parameters.name: requesterUserId
parameters.description: Platform user id (e.g. Discord snowflake) to resolve to a chat_member_mapping row. Required (and only used) in requester scope (i.e. when `scope` is omitted).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only used when `scope=admin`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Only used when `scope=admin`. Clamped server-side to 1-200.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Only used when `scope=admin`.

200.description: Scheduled messages for the resolved scope. `total`, `limit`, and `offset` are only present for `scope=admin`.

400.description: Missing/invalid `app`, an invalid `status` value (scope=admin), or an unresolvable `requesterUserId` (requester scope).

403.description: Role check failed for the requested scope: bot role required for `scope=bot`, admin role required for `scope=admin`, or bot/admin role required for requester scope. All checks are enforced in-handler (not via `requireAdmin`/`requireBotOrAdmin` middleware).

post.description: Requires the bot or admin role (checked in-handler). `requesterUserId` is resolved to a chat_member_mapping row and becomes the owner of the new row; the bot supplies it on behalf of the end user.

requesterUserId.description: Platform user id (e.g. Discord snowflake) resolved to a chat_member_mapping row.

scheduled_at.description: Any value parseable by `new Date(...)`; normalized to UTC ISO 8601.

400.description: Missing/invalid `app`, an unresolvable `requesterUserId`, missing `chat_channel_id`, missing `message_body`, or an invalid `scheduled_at`.

get.summary: Get one scheduled message by id
get.description: Requires the bot or admin role (checked in-handler via the same requester-resolution helper as the list/create/update/delete routes). The resolved requester must own the row.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: Chat app key. Currently only "discord" is supported.

parameters.name: requesterUserId
parameters.description: Platform user id (e.g. Discord snowflake) resolved to a chat_member_mapping row.

400.description: Invalid `id`, missing/invalid `app`, or an unresolvable `requesterUserId`.

403.description: Either the caller is not bot/admin, or the resolved requester does not own this scheduled message. Both checks are enforced in-handler.

put.summary: Update a scheduled message (requester edit, bot sent-mark, or admin override)
put.description:
`app` (query or body) is always required and is used to look up the existing row before branching on `scope`:
  - `scope=bot`: marks the row `status="sent"` (optionally with a
    `sent_at`, defaulting to now). Requires the bot role
    (checked in-handler). Used by the scheduler after dispatch.
  - `scope=admin`: updates `message_body` and/or `scheduled_at` on any
    row regardless of status. Requires the admin role (checked
    in-handler). At least one field must be provided.
  - Omitted (default, "requester scope"): resolves `requesterUserId`
    to a chat_member_mapping row, requires it to own the row, requires
    the row to still be `status="pending"`, and updates
    `message_body` and/or `scheduled_at`. Requires the bot or admin
    role (checked in-handler); at least one field must be provided.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: Chat app key. May be supplied here or in the request body; required either way.

requesterUserId.description: Platform user id (e.g. Discord snowflake) resolved to a chat_member_mapping row.

sent_at.description: Defaults to the current time when omitted.

400.description: Invalid `id`; missing/invalid `app`; for `scope=bot`, `status` was not `"sent"`; for `scope=admin` or requester scope, an empty `message_body`, an invalid `scheduled_at`, or neither field provided; for requester scope, an unresolvable `requesterUserId` or the row is no longer `status="pending"`.

403.description: Role check failed for the requested scope: bot role required for `scope=bot`, admin role required for `scope=admin`, bot/admin role required for requester scope, or (requester scope) the resolved requester does not own this row. All checks are enforced in-handler.

delete.summary: Delete a scheduled message (requester delete or admin override)
delete.description: `scope=admin` (query or body) deletes the row regardless of status and requires the admin role (checked in-handler). Otherwise (default, "requester scope") requires the bot or admin role (checked in-handler), resolves `requesterUserId` to a chat_member_mapping row, and only deletes the row when it is owned by that requester and still `status="pending"`.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: May also be supplied in the request body. Omit for requester scope.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: Chat app key. May be supplied here or in the request body; required for requester scope (not read for `scope=admin`).

parameters.name: requesterUserId
parameters.description: Platform user id (e.g. Discord snowflake) resolved to a chat_member_mapping row. Required for requester scope; may also be supplied in the request body.

400.description: Invalid `id`; or, for requester scope, missing/invalid `app` or an unresolvable `requesterUserId`.

403.description: Admin role required for `scope=admin`, or bot/admin role required for requester scope. Both checks are enforced in-handler.

404.description: Not found for `scope=admin`, or (requester scope) no pending row with this id is owned by the resolved requester.

post.summary: Record emoji usage in a message
post.description: Increments emoji_frequency / user_emoji_tracking for each emoji in the message. If isReply is true and the emojis are exactly one configured plusplus/minusminus emoji, also records a single +/- vote for repliedUserId instead of counting it as emoji usage.

authorId.description: Discord snowflake of the message author.

repliedUserId.description: Discord snowflake of the user being replied to.

200.description: Emoji usage recorded, or a reply vote applied. `ok` may be false with no `applied`/`error` when authorId or emojis were missing/empty.

applied.description: Present only when isReply triggered a single +/- vote instead of emoji counting.

400.description: Missing/invalid app parameter, or repliedUserId is not a known chat member.

post.summary: Record sticker usage in a message
post.description: Increments emoji_frequency (type='sticker') / user_emoji_tracking for each sticker in the message. Unlike emoji-count, there is no plus/minus branch — Discord has no reply-with-sticker vote mechanism.

authorId.description: Discord snowflake of the message author.

200.description: Sticker usage recorded. `ok` may be false with no `error` when authorId or stickers were missing/empty.

400.description: Missing/invalid app parameter, or authorId is not a known chat member.

post.summary: Parse a message or reaction for plus/minus votes
post.description: type defaults to "message" when omitted or not "reaction". "message" parses word++/word-- and @mention++/@mention-- tokens out of message.content and records one vote per match (self-votes on mentions are skipped). "reaction" records a single +/- vote directly.

voterId.description: Discord snowflake of the message author (voter).

recorded.description: Number of votes recorded (0 or 1 for reaction mode).

400.description: Missing/invalid app, missing voterId/targetUserId/reactorId, invalid value, or self-vote attempted.

post.summary: Record or withdraw a repost accusation
post.description: repost=1 upserts a row in user_repost_tracking keyed on (userid, msgid, accuser). repost=-1 deletes the row(s) for that (msgid, accuser).

userid.description: Discord snowflake of the message author accused of reposting.

msgid.description: Discord snowflake of the accused message.

accuser.description: Discord snowflake of the user who added the repost emoji.

deleted.description: Rows deleted; only present when action is withdrawn.

400.description: Missing/invalid app, userid/msgid/accuser missing, repost not 1 or -1, or unknown chat member.
